clarification.reason: Attempt 8 fell to 74.6%, especially confusing prepaid accounts with deposit accounts and vehicle financing with personal loans. Replace its rigid category order with direct contextual distinctions for those errors and the unchanged ten-label vocabulary.
clarification.instruction: Choose the one product category that best explains the consumer's relationship with the respondent. Use Mortgage for financing secured by a home; Student loan for education borrowing; Vehicle loan or lease for purchasing, financing, leasing, paying for, or repossessing a car or other vehicle. Use Payday loan, title loan, personal loan, or advance loan for non-education personal/installment borrowing, payday loans, cash advances, or cash borrowed against the title of an already-owned vehicle; do not call ordinary vehicle-purchase financing a personal or title loan merely because the narrative says loan. Use Credit card for a revolving card account and its purchase disputes, billing, interest, balance transfers, or rewards. Use Prepaid card for a stored-value, gift, reloadable, payroll, unemployment, tax-refund, or benefits-disbursement card and access to its balance; receiving a deposit or having an account number does not by itself turn such a card into a checking account. Use Checking or savings account for an ordinary bank deposit relationship and its balance, access, fees, checks, or debit-card servicing. Use Money transfer, virtual currency, or money service when the disputed relationship is a remittance, wire, payment-processing, electronic-transfer, wallet, or virtual-currency service. Use Debt collection when the respondent pursues or reports a collection debt. Use Credit reporting or other personal consumer reports when the respondent provides a credit bureau or consumer-reporting service. A secondary reference to another product, a payment destination, a statute, or a requested remedy does not override the main relationship.

diff: 1. [S01] Classify the complaint into the financial-product category provided by the company whose conduct is challenged. Prefer the most specific supported product, including a product identifiable from the respondent's role or specialization. Reporting by a creditor about its own card or loan remains that card or loan product; reporting by a debt collector remains Debt collection. Choose Credit reporting or other personal consumer reports for a credit bureau or consumer-reporting service, not simply because a consumer discusses a report, identity theft, or the FCRA. Identify the underlying service first, then apply the product definitions. <!-- pland:english -->

2. [S02] Read the complete evidence text supplied in this request and separate the consumer's concrete account or transaction facts from copied legal arguments, generic dispute templates, and requested remedies. Identify the named provider, the kind of account or agreement, what happened, and which service the consumer wants corrected. Give those factual details more weight than repeated terms in long statutory quotations. A loan or card account does not become a credit-reporting product merely because the consumer wants its entry deleted; a prepaid card does not become a transfer service merely because its funds were moved. Use a provider's stated role or clearly identifiable product specialization when the narrative omits the generic product name. Treat redaction placeholders as missing information rather than as evidence for a category. <!-- pland:english -->

-3. [S03] Choose exactly one label by resolving the most specific financial product supported by the narrative. First distinguish loans: home financing or mortgage servicing is Mortgage; education borrowing, including private education loans and tuition financing, is Student loan; vehicle-purchase financing, leasing, or repossession is Vehicle loan or lease; other personal/installment borrowing, payday borrowing, cash advances, and title-secured cash loans are Payday loan, title loan, personal loan, or advance loan. Next distinguish cards: borrowing through a card, billing, interest, rewards, or credit-card purchase disputes is Credit card; gift, stored-value, reloadable, payroll, or benefit cards are Prepaid card. For remaining cases, bank deposit-account access, balances, fees, checks, and debit-card servicing are Checking or savings account; a disputed remittance, wire, transfer execution, payment processor, wallet, or virtual-currency service is Money transfer, virtual currency, or money service. A complaint whose respondent acts as a collector or enforces a debt is Debt collection. A complaint about a credit bureau or consumer-reporting service itself is Credit reporting or other personal consumer reports. Apply these distinctions to the product or service under dispute, not to a background product, incidental payment destination, copied statute, or requested report deletion. <!-- pland:english -->

+3. [S03] Choose the one product category that best explains the consumer's relationship with the respondent. Use Mortgage for financing secured by a home; Student loan for education borrowing; Vehicle loan or lease for purchasing, financing, leasing, paying for, or repossessing a car or other vehicle. Use Payday loan, title loan, personal loan, or advance loan for non-education personal/installment borrowing, payday loans, cash advances, or cash borrowed against the title of an already-owned vehicle; do not call ordinary vehicle-purchase financing a personal or title loan merely because the narrative says loan. Use Credit card for a revolving card account and its purchase disputes, billing, interest, balance transfers, or rewards. Use Prepaid card for a stored-value, gift, reloadable, payroll, unemployment, tax-refund, or benefits-disbursement card and access to its balance; receiving a deposit or having an account number does not by itself turn such a card into a checking account. Use Checking or savings account for an ordinary bank deposit relationship and its balance, access, fees, checks, or debit-card servicing. Use Money transfer, virtual currency, or money service when the disputed relationship is a remittance, wire, payment-processing, electronic-transfer, wallet, or virtual-currency service. Use Debt collection when the respondent pursues or reports a collection debt. Use Credit reporting or other personal consumer reports when the respondent provides a credit bureau or consumer-reporting service. A secondary reference to another product, a payment destination, a statute, or a requested remedy does not override the main relationship. <!-- pland:english -->

4. [S04] Before returning the label, check that it describes the disputed financial product rather than merely a law, symptom, or requested remedy. If choosing Credit reporting or other personal consumer reports, verify that the complaint concerns a bureau or reporting service rather than the named lender's loan, card, or a collector's debt. If choosing Money transfer, virtual currency, or money service, verify that executing or processing the transfer is itself disputed rather than merely the way funds left a prepaid card or deposit account. For a purchase-charge or billing dispute, distinguish a credit-card borrowing account from a debit card tied to an explicitly identified deposit account; the word bank alone does not establish the latter. Resolve the choice using the narrative's strongest product evidence, then return exactly one JSON object shaped as {"label":"<known bucket>"} with no explanation or additional fields. <!-- pland:english -->
